claims.text: Cohesity FortKnox supports AIX Server [1]
FortKnox supports vaulting or recovering AIX Server workloads [2]
FortKnox can archive a full backup to a cloud vault for AIX [3]
FortKnox can archive an incremental backup to a cloud vault for AIX [4]
FortKnox supports Physical Server backup/archival workflows covering AIX [5]
Veeam Backup & Replication protects computers running IBM AIX [6]
VBR supports IBM AIX servers, collectively called Unix servers/machines [7]
Veeam Agents offer backup and recovery for IBM AIX servers and workstations [8]
Veeam Agents protect physical or virtual machines running IBM AIX [9]
Documented for: Cohesity
Documented for: Veeam

A.notes: Citation [2] source only lists AIX as a supported vaulting workload; it says nothing about recovery (the workflow table even shows Recover = No for AIX). Veeam gold counted present: agent-based AIX protection managed from VBR is stated, though the file-level/LPAR detail is not.

claims.text: Veeam Agent for IBM AIX is a data protection and DR solution for AIX machines [1]
Supports file-level backup of directories and files to local/external drives, network shares or a Veeam repository [1][4]
Can be integrated with Veeam Backup & Replication [1]
Requires 1 GB RAM (4 GB for bare metal recovery), 1.5 GB disk, 10 Mbps network [2][3][4]
Supported OS: AIX 6.1 (experimental) and 7.1-7.3 TL3 [3][4]
Backup of VIOS and clustered systems (incl. PowerHA SystemMirror) not supported [2][3][4]

B.notes: Says only 'No other vendors are mentioned' without naming Microsoft, AWS or Cohesity, so those gold facts are absent; Cohesity is documented per the gold but missed.

claims.text: Microsoft 365 Backup is pay-as-you-go, charged on consumption, unlike user-based licenses [2]
Billing set up through Azure subscription, resource group, region; owner/contributor role needed [6]
Departmental billing segments costs into different Azure subscriptions via multiple billing policies [6][8]
Veeam licensed per backed-up user account; each consumes one unit; restores need no license [1]
Units consumed by mailboxes, OneDrive accounts, SharePoint personal sites backed up in the last 31 days [1]
Subscription license: paid, 1-5 year term [1][4]
Rental license: paid, ~1 month, service providers only [1][3]
Not For Resale license: free, for demos/training [1]
Evaluation license: free, for testing [1]
Without a license runs in Community Edition: 10 users, 1 TB SharePoint, 10 teams [1][5]

A.notes: Gold 3 absent: never says a unit is revoked after 31 days without backup, or that Teams objects and group/non-personal sites don't consume units.

claims.text: Microsoft 365 Backup is pay-as-you-go, consumption-based rather than seat-based [9]
Backup Storage application tied to pay-as-you-go billing via a Billing Policy [11]
Active Backup Storage Controller is responsible for billing in the Consuming Tenant [12][13]
Charged on user-facing size of protected OneDrive accounts incl. first-stage recycle bin [14]
Charged on size of live mailboxes plus online archives [15]
Cost breakdowns for OneDrive, Exchange, SharePoint [2][3][4]
Departmental billing is supported [10]
Admin center usage reports exclude second-stage recycle bins and online archives, which must be calculated with PowerShell [5][6][7]
Get-MailboxStatistics can estimate online archive sizes [8]
Veeam licensed per protected user account, one unit each [16]
All users who are members of or have access to a backed-up team or non-personal SharePoint sites must be licensed [21]
Subscription and Rental licenses; auto update + usage reporting doubles the allowed overage [20][22]
Rental license for service providers, ~1 month term [17]
Free Not For Resale license for demos and training [18]
Microsoft charges by protected storage consumption, Veeam by protected user accounts [9][14][16]

B.notes: The source behind [5][6][7] only introduces the usage reports and does not mention the excluded recycle bins/archives or PowerShell. Gold 0 lacks the Azure subscription; gold 1 lacks 'restores need no license'; gold 2 is missing entirely.
